items.claim: HTTP request smuggling arises where a front-end and back-end disagree on where a request ends, so a smuggled request is prepended to the next legitimate user's request.
items.body:
In practice on HTB this shows up as:  [https://portswigger.net/web-security/request-smuggling](https://portswigger.net/web-security/request-smuggling)

Write-up provenance: zweilosec/htb-writeups :: linux-machines/hard/quick-write-up.md (7325 words, classified network).
items.disproof: Refuted when a front end rejects ambiguous framing outright, or when both hops agree on message boundaries for the same request, leaving no request to smuggle.
